title: Letters in the search location's own path count as matches, so typo-only results are not dropped
problem: The check that separates real matches from typo-tolerant ones (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:566-580) tests each word against `shown`, which is the path relative to the scope, or the full absolute path when the search is 'This Computer' (571-575). fff only ever matched the path inside the search location (docs/manual.md:356 says the same), so the location's own prefix, such as `/Users/alice` or `/home/user`, supplies letters fff never saw. Any word that is a subsequence of that prefix (`users`, `user`, `home`, the account name, and chance words such as `slice` or `rice` for alice) passes `strict` for every hit. With Allow typos off, typo-only matches therefore still show for those words, against docs/manual.md:997. With it on, they are never dropped (578-580). In a multi-word search such as `alice resume`, the name stops narrowing anything. The same absolute path feeds the depth penalty (`hit.path.components().count()`, 1534), so with two search locations at different depths, such as home and /Volumes/Work/Clients, equal matches in the deeper location lose 3 points per extra level.
proposal: Give RawHit a `rel: String`: the item's path inside its root as fff returned it, minus the scope's relative prefix when scoped. Set it at the construction sites in search_root (708, 719-725, 732, 747-753); app_hits (1468) uses the display name. In Engine::search make `strict` test `hit.rel.to_lowercase()` in place of the absolute path. In rerank compute `depth` from `rel` (number of '/'-separated parts) and make app_hits' compensation at 1467-1468 use the same count.
original_test_plan: Engine test: root directory named `budget-box-<pid>` containing `bduget.txt`; set settings.typos = false; the names for `budget` must be empty (today it returns bduget.txt, because `budget` is found in the root's name). With typos on, add `budget.txt` and assert the names for `budget` == [budget.txt]. Unit test: two RawHits with equal fff scores and the same relative path under roots of different depth get equal rerank scores.
original_risks: Changing the depth base shifts every score by a constant within one root (harmless) and re-balances roots against each other; the depth half can be left out if only the typo fix is wanted. Tests build RawHit::file directly (1868-1869, 2242), so the constructor needs a default `rel` derived from the path. The typo-fallback-near-miss candidate is best done after this one.

verifier.claim_check:
The typo half is TRUE, and wider than the candidate says. The depth half is true but should be dropped.

Typo check (confirmed by reading the code, not run):
- crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:569-580: `strict` tests each word against `hit.path.strip_prefix(req.scope)`, falling back to the whole absolute `hit.path` when there is no scope. There is no other filter: `settings.typos` is read only at 578 and never passed to fff.
- `hit.path` is `join_rel(&base, fff_rel)` (705, 718, 732, 744), so the root's own path is in the string being tested.
- fff matches only the root-relative path (fff-search-0.11.0 src/score.rs:41-51 and 195-198) and always allows at least 2 typos (src/file_picker.rs:1113, `(len/4).clamp(2,6)`). The strict check is therefore the only thing keeping near misses out.
- This is the default setup: scope defaults to `SearchScope::Computer` (src/finder/mod.rs:549) and the default root is Home (docs/manual.md:1050), so every default search is tested against `/Users/<name>/...` or `/home/<name>/...`.
- Wider than claimed: the word does not have to sit wholly in the prefix. Any leading letters found in the root path are consumed there. With root `/home/user`, `music` passes strict for `basic.txt` (m, u, s from the prefix), so the near miss is kept even when `music.mp3` exists.
- Overstated: in `alice resume`, fff still narrows by `alice` with typo tolerance (score.rs:89-105); only the strict requirement on that word is lost.
- Not intentional: docs/manual.md:356 says letters must appear "in the path inside the search location"; :360 and :997 say typo-only matches are dropped. The check dates from commit b3dfed4 with no comment claiming the absolute path is wanted.
- No test pins it. `typos_can_be_turned_off` (engine.rs:2047) passes only because `/tmp/fff-typos-<pid>/` has no `b`. The searches in tests/controls.rs:336-345, tests/finder.rs:75 and tests/server.rs:106-141 give the same results either way.
- Side effect of the same code on Windows: when fff's base spelling differs from the root (engine.rs:87-97), `strip_prefix(scope)` fails and scoped searches also fall back to the absolute path.

Depth half:
- engine.rs:1534 does count absolute components, so roots at different depths differ by 3 points per level.
- That is tiny next to the 40-160 point name bonuses (1516-1533).
- `app_hits` cancels the same absolute count (1467-1468), and the app-before-file ordering is documented (manual.md:360) and tested (engine.rs:2193, 2249).
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do the typo half only. Leave `rerank` (engine.rs:1507-1536) and the compensation in `app_hits` (1467-1468) untouched.

1. `RawHit` (1338-1374): add `rel: String`, the lowercased path inside the searched location. Keep the `RawHit::file` / `RawHit::dir` signatures and initialise `rel` to `String::new()`. Add a small setter, e.g. `fn inside(mut self, rel: String) -> RawHit`. The callers at 846 (recents), 1868-1869 and 2242 (tests) never reach the strict check, so they need no change.

2. `search_root` (605-758): `scope_rel` already exists at 623-627, '/'-separated. Add a closure:
   `let inside = |rel: &str| { let rel = rel.trim_end_matches('/'); scope_rel.as_deref().and_then(|s| rel.strip_prefix(s)).and_then(|r| r.strip_prefix('/')).unwrap_or(rel).to_lowercase() };`
   Apply it at all four construction sites:
   - 708 (Folder search): `rel` is already bound.
   - 718 and 744: `relative_path(picker)` returns a `String` that is passed straight to `join_rel`; bind it to a local first.
   - 728-732 (mixed dir): `rel` is already bound.
   `in_scope` (682-688) already guarantees the path starts with the scope, so the prefix strip always applies when scoped. For ad hoc indexes and scope == root, `scope_rel` is `None` and fff's rel is used as is.

3. `app_hits` (1447-1471): set `rel` to the lowercased display name already computed at 1452. Apps then pass strict by construction, as they do today.

4. `Engine::search` (569-577): delete `base`; `strict` becomes `|hit: &RawHit| words.iter().all(|w| is_subsequence(w, &hit.rel))`. Keep 578-580 as is. This also removes the two `to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()` calls per hit.

5. CHANGELOG.md: add a `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]` (the file currently has only Added and Changed there). docs/manual.md already describes the intended behaviour at 356, 360 and 997, so it needs no edit.

Pitfalls:
- Keep stripping the scope's own prefix for folder-scoped searches. That is today's behaviour whenever `strip_prefix` succeeds; do not switch scoped searches to the root-relative path.
- Use fff's '/'-separated rel string, not a `Path`. A word such as `src/main` then passes on Windows too.
- Do not add the proposed "default rel derived from the path" in the constructors. It would bring the absolute path back for any site that forgets the setter. An empty default fails closed.
verifier.test_plan:
Engine unit test in the `mod tests` of crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, modelled on `typos_can_be_turned_off` (2047-2081). No UI harness is needed.

Setup:
- Root: `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("budget-box-{}", std::process::id()))`.
- Create BOTH `budget.txt` and `bduget.txt` before `Engine::new`. `watch` is false, so the candidate's "add budget.txt later" step would not be indexed.
- `EngineOptions { roots: vec![dir.clone()], app_dirs: Vec::new(), db_dir: None, watch: false, search: Default::default() }`, then `wait_ready(Duration::from_secs(10))`.
- Same `names` closure as the existing test (`files_only: true`, `limit: 50`).

Assertions:
- Typos on: `names("budget") == ["budget.txt"]`. Today both files come back, because `budget` is found in the root's name.
- Typos on: `names("bduget") == ["bduget.txt"]`. Today both come back.
- After `settings.typos = false; engine.set_search_settings(settings)`: `names("bugdet")` is empty. Today both files come back: b, u, g come from `budget-box` and d, e, t from the file name.
- A scoped search with `scope: Some(dir.clone())` gives the same names as the unscoped one. This already holds today and guards the scoped path.
- Remove the directory at the end.

Existing tests that must stay green (I could not run cargo; this is from reading them):
- engine.rs: `typos_can_be_turned_off`, `quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter`, `searches_a_folder`, `finds_apps_without_indexing_them`, `one_letter_app_hits_dont_flood`, `rerank_prefers_name_matches`.
- tests/controls.rs `search_scope_button` (`ui.names() == ["Budget.csv"]`), tests/finder.rs `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing`, tests/server.rs find assertions.

The candidate's second test (equal rerank scores under roots of different depth) goes away with the depth half.
verifier.risks:
Typo half: low risk.
- It only removes near-miss rows that the root's own letters let through. With Allow typos on, a search with no strict match still shows the fallback list.
- Top results do not move, because rerank is untouched. Users will see shorter result tails for affected queries.
- The new test assumes fff returns a transposed name as a typo match. The existing test at engine.rs:2074 shows this for `bduget` -> `budget.txt`. The empty-list assertion holds whatever fff returns.

Depth half: drop it.
- Apps keep a net zero depth penalty, so basing depth on the root-relative path lifts every home file by 3 x (root depth) relative to apps: 9 points for /Users/name, 15 or more in the temp-dir test.
- That can flip the documented Safari/Terminal-before-file ordering (docs/manual.md:360) and the assertion at engine.rs:2193. The margin depends on fff's file score, which I could not check without running.
- The gain is at most a few points between roots of different depth.

Nothing here was run; all of the above is from reading the code.
